name: Rivanna Station
tagline: The Army's ground intelligence hub, in the hills just north of Charlottesville, Virginia.
_note: Army intelligence site (NGIC, plus DIA and NGA in the Joint-Use Intelligence Analysis Facility), a sub-installation of Fort Belvoir in Albemarle County VA (Eastern time). Built 2026-11-04 at Chris's request. CONUS full template: BAH MHA VA295 Charlottesville (duty ZIP 22911; rates read from the official DoD 2026 table, not typed). No on-post housing, barracks, commissary, exchange or military clinic; CDC on site (Belvoir MWR page updated 2026-11-10). Sources: army.mil (2010 JUIAF opening, 2019 NGIC workforce ~2,500), Belvoir HSO, TRICARE Prime Remote, CAAR Q3 2026 market report (rechecked 2026-11-10), Virginia School Quality Profiles 2025-26 (rechecked 2026-11-10), Albemarle/Lakeside MS fact sheet. Medium-confidence flags: coords approximate (OpenStreetMap NGIC building); drive times are routing estimates; JAG School exchange shop comes from a 2021 Defense Affairs Committee welcome packet and is now worded as unconfirmed; hospital renamed Alexander T. Augusta Military Medical Center; Prime Remote claim removed (depends on ZIP); sales tax vote added (unofficial results); Prime Remote eligibility depends on the home ZIP; Albemarle school feeder pattern from an undated fact sheet.

data.Branch: U.S. Army (a sub-installation of Fort Belvoir)
data.Location: Albemarle County, Virginia, on US-29 about 12 miles north of downtown Charlottesville

sections.title: Mission & Identity
data: Rivanna Station is home to the National Ground Intelligence Center (NGIC), part of the Army's Intelligence and Security Command. NGIC produces the Army's intelligence on foreign ground forces and their equipment. The Defense Intelligence Agency and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency also work here, in the Joint-Use Intelligence Analysis Facility that opened in 2010.
It is a small, secure site run as a sub-installation of Fort Belvoir, about two hours north. There is no big garrison around it, so daily life happens in Charlottesville and the surrounding counties.

source.label: Army.mil: DIA opens new facility at Rivanna Station (2010)

sections.title: Where to Live: City, County or North of the Gate

data.subtitle: Rivanna has no on-post housing and no big base around it, so where you live is the big decision. The closest and least expensive homes are often north of the gate, not in Charlottesville itself.
intro: Charlottesville is a pricey market for a military town. In the third quarter of 2026 the median home sold for $550,000 in Albemarle County, $495,000 in the City of Charlottesville and $400,000 in Greene County, according to the Charlottesville Area Association of Realtors. Greene's median fell 3% from a year earlier while its listings rose 38%, so buyers there have more room to negotiate.

Rivanna Station sits on US-29 about 12 miles north of downtown. Northern Albemarle neighborhoods are 5 to 15 minutes from the gate, and Greene County's Ruckersville is about 13 minutes north, so the lower-cost county is also one of the closest.

On November 3, 2026, Albemarle and Charlottesville voters approved a 1% school sales tax (unofficial results), raising the rate from 5.3% to 6.3%. Neither start date is set; in Albemarle the earliest likely start is May 1, 2027. Greene and Fluvanna voters rejected it.

recommendations.advice: Northern Albemarle neighborhoods like Hollymead and Forest Lakes are minutes from the gate, with Albemarle County schools.
Greene County (Ruckersville) has the lowest home prices and real estate tax rate ($0.70 per $100) of the three, keeps 5.3% sales tax after voters rejected the increase, and is about 13 minutes away.
Living in Charlottesville puts you near UVA and the Downtown Mall, about 23 minutes from the gate.

Check the exact schools for any address. In Virginia's 2025-26 ratings, 8 of Albemarle's 24 schools (33%) and 1 of Greene's 5 (20%) were Distinguished, both below the 44% statewide. Near the gate, Lakeside Middle is Distinguished and Albemarle High Approaching Expectations; in Greene, William Monroe Middle is Approaching Expectations and William Monroe High Distinguished.

source.label: CAAR Q3 2026 Housing Market Report; Virginia School Quality Profiles (2025-26)

sections.title: Gates & Access
data: Rivanna Station is a secure intelligence site, not an open post, and its buildings are not open to the public. Your sponsor or unit will explain how access works for you.
Don't plan on bringing family or guests onto the site. Most of the services a family uses are off post anyway.

source.label: Army.mil: DIA opens new facility at Rivanna Station (2010)

sections.title: On-Base Housing
data: Rivanna Station has no family housing or barracks. The site is a few office buildings and parking, so everyone lives off post and rents or buys in the local market.
Fort Belvoir, Rivanna's parent installation, runs a Housing Services Office that offers off-post housing counseling and rental referrals by phone (703-805-3019).

source.label: DoD 2026 BAH Rates, MHA VA295 (Charlottesville, VA)

sections.title: Schools
data: There are no DoDEA schools here; children attend the local public schools. Your address decides the district: Albemarle County Public Schools around the station, Charlottesville City Schools inside the city, or Greene County Public Schools to the north.

Closest to the gate, northern Albemarle is served by Baker-Butler, Hollymead and Stony Point elementary schools, Lakeside Middle and Albemarle High (Stony Point has two pathways, and only one goes through Lakeside). Boundaries change, so confirm the zone for any address with ACPS Transportation, (434) 973-5716.

Virginia rates every school each fall. In the 2025-26 ratings, released in October 2026, 44% of schools statewide were Distinguished; Lakeside Middle was Distinguished and Albemarle High Approaching Expectations; Greene's William Monroe Middle was Approaching Expectations and William Monroe High Distinguished. Look up the rating for the specific schools that serve a neighborhood before you sign.

source.label: Virginia School Quality Profiles (2025-26); ACPS attendance zones

data.Clinic: None on post. The nearest military hospital is Alexander T. Augusta Military Medical Center (formerly Fort Belvoir Community Hospital) at Fort Belvoir, about 2 hours north.
data.Care: Most families use civilian doctors. UVA Health and Sentara Martha Jefferson Hospital are the main local hospitals.
data.TRICARE: East region (Humana Military). TRICARE Prime Remote is available in designated ZIP codes far from a military hospital or clinic; check your home ZIP with the TRICARE Plan Finder before you choose a plan.

source.label: TRICARE Prime Remote and East Region (official); Alexander T. Augusta Military Medical Center

data.Commissary: None at Rivanna. The nearest are at MCB Quantico, Fort Belvoir and Fort Gregg-Adams, each about 2 to 2.5 hours away.
data.Exchange: None at Rivanna. A small exchange outlet at the JAG School in Charlottesville has been reported, but we could not confirm it is open. Full exchanges are at the same bases as the commissaries.

data.On site: Rivanna Station Child Development Center, 2425 Defense Way
data.Hours: Monday to Friday, 6:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.
data.Tip: Request care early on MilitaryChildCare.com, and call the center to confirm openings.

intro: Whether to rent or buy is the biggest money decision of most PCS moves. In Charlottesville, home prices are well above most military markets, so the stakes are higher than usual.
rent: Your tour is about three years or less, or your orders feel uncertain.
You want time to learn the city, the county and Greene County before committing.
You'd rather not gamble on resale timing in a high-priced market when you PCS out.
Your BAH covers rent in the area you'd choose.
buy: You expect to stay four years or more.
You want to use your VA loan and build equity instead of paying rent.
A home in Greene County or northern Albemarle fits your budget.
You've found a neighborhood and commute you're confident about.
data.bottom_line: Charlottesville's prices make buying a bigger commitment than at most bases. Run your BAH against the rent and home prices above, weigh your tour length, and talk to a lender and an agent who work with military families before you commit.

intro: The first month at a small site with no big base nearby is mostly about setting up off post. Knocking these out early makes everything else easier.

steps.title: Line up temporary lodging
steps.text: There's no lodging on Rivanna Station, so book a hotel or short-term rental near US-29 before you arrive. You can claim Temporary Lodging Expense (TLE) for a limited number of days while you house-hunt.

steps.title: In-process and update DEERS
steps.text: Report to your unit, and make sure DEERS and ID cards are current for every family member. ID card appointments are limited locally, so book one early.

steps.title: Start your home search
steps.text: Call Fort Belvoir's Housing Services Office for off-post counseling, and decide early between the city, northern Albemarle County and Greene County.

steps.title: Sort out vehicle taxes
steps.text: Virginia counties and cities tax vehicles every year. If your legal residence is outside Virginia, file for the military exemption with your county or city: Albemarle asks for an LES or commanding officer's statement every year, Charlottesville your most recent LES and Fluvanna a January LES. Greene publishes no steps, so call its Commissioner of the Revenue at 434-985-5211.

steps.title: Enroll the kids in school
steps.text: Your address decides the district: Albemarle County, Charlottesville City or Greene County. Contact the district early and bring records and immunizations.

steps.title: Set up healthcare
steps.text: Check whether your home ZIP qualifies for TRICARE Prime Remote, then pick a civilian primary care doctor in the TRICARE East network.

data.a: It's home to the National Ground Intelligence Center (NGIC), the Army's center for intelligence on foreign ground forces. The Defense Intelligence Agency and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency also work there.
No. Rivanna Station has no family housing or barracks, so everyone lives off post. Fort Belvoir's Housing Services Office offers off-post counseling by phone.

Mostly in northern Albemarle County (Hollymead, Forest Lakes), Greene County (Ruckersville) or the City of Charlottesville. Greene is the least expensive of the three and about 13 minutes from the gate.

data.q: Is there a commissary or military hospital?
data.a: No. The nearest military hospital, Alexander T. Augusta Military Medical Center at Fort Belvoir, is about 2 hours away, and the nearest commissaries are at bases a similar drive away. Families use civilian doctors through TRICARE; check whether your ZIP qualifies for TRICARE Prime Remote.
Rivanna Station is MHA VA295 (Charlottesville). Use the calculator above for your grade.

data.q: Is the sales tax going up?
data.a: In Albemarle and Charlottesville, yes. Voters approved a 1% sales tax for school construction on November 3, 2026 (unofficial results), taking the rate from 5.3% to 6.3%. Neither start date is set. In Albemarle the earliest likely start is May 1, 2027, if supervisors adopt the ordinance in December, and the tax ends June 30, 2046; Charlottesville had not set a date when we checked. Greene and Fluvanna voters rejected it, so their rate stays 5.3%.

data.q: Is the JAG School the same place?
data.a: No. The Army's Judge Advocate General's Legal Center and School is a separate site next to UVA's law school, about 11 miles south of Rivanna Station.
